minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard IT and Police FY25 budgets, approved a grant-writer letter, and debated an override article.
minutes.summary: The committee heard FY25 budget presentations from the IT director and the police chief, including a second lieutenant and an admin assistant hours increase. It voted by roll call to send a letter to the Select Board supporting contracted grant-writing services. A long discussion followed on a possible override warrant article, the school committee's multiple budget scenarios, and property valuations.

public_comment.topic: Said he nearly filed an open meeting law complaint over last week's override discussion and vote not being on the agenda, and asked for dollar impacts on taxpayers including debt exclusions.

votes.motion: Approve the revised grant-writing services letter and send it to the select board, authorizing the chair to send it.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted a large percentage increase in the line for the IT admin assistant, whose hours would go from 16 to 32 and become benefit-eligible.
Member walked through FY23, FY24 and requested figures; the director said the earlier jump included network equipment and replacement is aimed at about a tenth of the fleet a year.
The chief said the stated increase omitted the patrol officers' contract raise, so the true increase is lower than shown.
The request for the comfort dog's care was not funded this year.
A member asked about the gap between request and preliminary budget; the chief tied the difference to the comfort dog and said the budget as presented meets needs.
The letter cites a line in the preliminary budget for contracted grant-writing services.
A member relayed four school scenarios, from the town manager's preliminary figure to level services with all FY24 positions.
Members worked a rough example of an override as a share of the levy and the effect on a tax bill.

transfers.description: Possible transfer from another line to the meetings/conferences line after members attended MMA; line is about a thousand dollars.

decisions.decision: The grant-writer letter would be read as communication at the Select Board meeting, and the chair would send it to the select board chair.
Chair will bring town-side numbers verified with department heads to next week's meeting.
Chair will add the town manager's borrowing-projects meeting to next week's agenda.
Chair will invite the school facilities director to the public hearing.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted unanimously by roll call to send the Select Board a letter supporting contracted grant-writing services.
The committee heard the police chief's FY25 budget; the chief said the shown increase leaves out the patrol officers' contract raise, so the true increase is lower.
The IT director presented an FY25 budget that includes raising the IT admin assistant from part-time hours to a benefit-eligible schedule.
Members discussed a possible override warrant article and the school committee's four budget scenarios, but reached no resolution.
The request to fund the comfort dog's care was not funded in the preliminary police budget.

why_it_matters: The unresolved override discussion and the school's four budget scenarios bear on whether residents will be asked to vote on a Proposition 2.5 override and how much it could add to a tax bill.
A resident at public comment asked for the dollar impact on taxpayers, including debt exclusions, and members only worked a rough example, so a firm bill figure has not yet been put on the record.
watch_next: Next week's meeting: the chair is to bring town-side numbers verified with department heads and add the town manager's borrowing-projects meeting to the agenda.
The public hearing, to which the chair is to invite the school facilities director.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the one non-procedural vote (the grant-writer letter, unanimous roll call) and on the school override percentages and the $20,000 police gap. They differ in the figures: the IT hardware maintenance amount ($30,000 officially vs 29,000 in ours), the comfort dog amount ($199,000 vs $19,095.09), and whether the clerk was present (official says absent, ours lists a member by a similar name), plus several decisions and a possible transfer recorded by only one side.
